slides.say: In triangle A B C, the marked angle outside the triangle and the interior angle at A are vertical angles. Based on this information and the information in the figure, what is the value of x?

We need x. Inside the triangle we know two angles, four x at B and five x at C. The third angle, at A, is missing, but there's a three x right next to it, outside the triangle. [short pause] So first we'll find the angle at A, and then we'll use the angle sum of a triangle.

[short pause] Look at point A. Two straight lines cross there, the line of side A B, and the line of side A C, which goes on past A. When two lines cross, the angles facing each other are vertical angles, and vertical angles are equal. So the angle inside the triangle at A is also three x.
at: So the angle inside the triangle

slides.say: Now the angle sum. The three angles of a triangle always add up to one hundred eighty. So three x, plus four x, plus five x, equals one hundred eighty.
at: The three angles of a triangle
So three x, plus four x

slides.say: Three x plus four x plus five x is twelve x. Twelve x equals one hundred eighty, so x is one hundred eighty divided by twelve. Twelve times fifteen is one hundred eighty, so x is fifteen. Choice number two is our answer.
at: Choice number two is our answer
